description: Verify that DUT replies to an ARP Request whose target_ip equals DUT's own IP — the only essential trigger condition for an ARP Reply (RFC 826 §2.4)
approach:
[Objective]
The one criterion that must be checked on the receive path: target_ip == iface IP. This case is the positive control for ARP_37 (target_ip != DUT IP, no reply expected).

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: ARP Request injected
   • opcode      = 1
   • target_ip   = DUT IP   ← matches
   • sender_*    = HOST-1-IP / MAC-ADDR1

2. Observation (3 s window):
   • DUT → Tester: ARP Reply (opcode 2, sender_mac=DUT, target_ip=HOST-1-IP)

[Pass condition]
DUT emits an ARP Reply within the observation window.

[Fail condition]
Fail_no_reply — DUT did not reply despite target_ip matching DUT's own IP. Indicates a fundamental ARP reception failure.

verdicts.Pass: DUT replied to a Request whose target_ip matched — normal
verdicts.Fail_no_reply: DUT did not reply despite target_ip match — fundamental reception failure
